subject: [PATCH] memcg: trim the per-cpu charge stock instead of draining it

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Michal Hocko suggested modifying the patch to preserve the maximum stock size by setting MEMCG_STOCK_HIGH := MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH and MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH := MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH / 2, which would prevent all-or-nothing behavior in charging and reduce the impact on the charging path.
reviews.raw_body:
The idea is sound. I would just not increase the overall stock size in
the same patch. Fine tuning can be done independently and ideally with
some numbers.
Would it make sense to start with MEMCG_STOCK_HIGH := MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH 
and  MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH := MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH / 2. That would preserve
the maximum stock size while preventing all or nothing behavior which is
indeed suboptimal and pushing charging path to a slower path way too
aggressively.

WDYT?

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a potential issue with the original patch, agreed to re-run an experiment with the suggested change, and plans to resubmit the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, this makes sense. Let me run the experiment with that workload to make sure
the newer number works and resend the patch.

Thanks for the review.

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Joshua Hahn questioned the logic behind draining the per-cpu charge stock when nr_pages exceeds the batch size, suggesting that sequential uncharges are uncommon due to batching in uncharge_gather.

Reviewer Joshua Hahn suggested correcting a typo in the patch by changing MEMCG_STOCK_HIGH to be calculated as MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH / 2, which would always drain the stock to this level when returning too many pages.
reviews.raw_body:
To be honest I never really understood why returning the stock and
making the nr_pages go over the batch size completely drained the stock.
One theory that I had was that if one uncharging is indicative that there
will be more future uncharges coming and we want to make room for those
uncharges to deposit their stocks, but now that I'm looking through the
code I'm pretty sure that sequential stock uncharges are not that
common, since we use uncharge_gather to batch up the LRU batch uncharging
area.

---

I like this idea and I think you meant { MEMCG_CHARGE_LOW :=
MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH / 2 } right? That way the only new change we
reintroduce is to always drain to a level when we return too many
pages to the stock.

Have a great day, Michal and Shakeel!
Joshua

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch modifies the per-cpu charge stock in Linux's memory cgroup (memcg) to trim excess pages instead of draining them completely. This change addresses a performance issue where certain applications would spend an excessive amount of time charging and uncharging pages due to a corner case in the memcg code. The patch introduces two new watermarks, MEMCG_STOCK_LOW and MEMCG_STOCK_HIGH, which are used to determine when to trim excess pages from the per-cpu charge stock. This approach is similar to how the page allocator manages its own percpu caches. As a result of this change, peak cached pages per memcg will increase from 64 to 96.
